questions.subTopic: CVP Analysis, BEP and Margin of Safety
questions.question:
A company produces a single product. Selling price is Rs. 100 per unit, Variable cost is Rs. 60 per unit, and Fixed cost is Rs. 12,00,000 per annum. Present sales volume is 40,000 units.
Calculate:
(a) P/V Ratio
(b) Break-even Point in units and in rupees
(c) Margin of Safety in rupees
(d) Sales required to earn a profit of Rs. 6,00,000.
questions.answer:
Marginal Costing Computations:

(a) P/V Ratio: Contribution per unit = Rs. 100 - Rs. 60 = Rs. 40. P/V Ratio = (Contribution / Selling Price) x 100 = (40 / 100) x 100 = 40%.

(b) Break-even Point (BEP): BEP (units) = Fixed Cost / Contribution per unit = Rs. 12,00,000 / Rs. 40 = 30,000 units. BEP (Value) = 30,000 x Rs. 100 = Rs. 30,00,000.

(c) Margin of Safety (MOS): Total Sales = 40,000 x Rs. 100 = Rs. 40,00,000. MOS = Total Sales - BEP Sales = Rs. 40,00,000 - Rs. 30,00,000 = Rs. 10,00,000 (or 10,000 units).

(d) Required Sales for Profit of Rs. 6,00,000: Required Sales = (Fixed Cost + Desired Profit) / P/V Ratio = (Rs. 12,00,000 + Rs. 6,00,000) / 0.40 = Rs. 45,00,000 (or 45,000 units).

questions.question: Material Price Variance is calculated as:
options: (Standard Quantity - Actual Quantity) x Standard Price
(Standard Price - Actual Price) x Actual Quantity
(Standard Price - Actual Price) x Standard Quantity
(Standard Quantity for Actual Output - Actual Quantity) x Actual Price
questions.reason: Material Price Variance (MPV) = Actual Quantity x (Standard Price - Actual Price). It measures the difference between standard price expected and actual price paid for material consumed.
